items.question: What can you throw in C# versus JavaScript?
items.answer: C# throw requires a System.Exception (or derived). JavaScript throw accepts any value, including strings and objects, which makes catch typing guesswork. On the CLR the thrown object carries a stack trace, HRESULT mapping, and serialization-friendly properties. Uncaught exceptions kill the thread; in a process with a default host they can take down the process.

Where do unobserved Task exceptions show up?
items.sixtySeconds: Throw Exception types only. JS can throw anything. Unobserved tasks are module 13.

items.question: When do you catch in an SQS worker versus letting it bubble?
items.answer: Catch at the message boundary when you can log, retry with backoff, or send to a DLQ and complete the receive. Catching Exception and swallowing leaves poison messages looping or silent data loss. Framework and host-level handlers exist for unhandled exceptions; bubbling is correct when you cannot restore state. Use when filters to catch transient faults without hiding bugs.
followUps: Where does finally run relative to a rethrow?
items.sixtySeconds: Worker boundary: recover, retry, DLQ. Unknown failures bubble. Do not empty-catch Exception.

items.question: throw versus throw ex versus wrapping?
items.answer: throw; rethrows the current exception and keeps the stack. throw ex; starts a new throw site and you lose the original frames — the classic bug. Wrapping is new OuterException(message, inner) when the caller needs a domain-level type plus the root cause. Never wrap just to log; log and throw; or wrap once at a boundary.
followUps: Why is catch (Exception) { throw; } sometimes still wrong?
items.sixtySeconds: throw; keeps the stack. throw ex; destroys it. Wrap with InnerException at boundaries.

items.question: How do you dispose a SkiaSharp SKSurface correctly?
items.answer: SKSurface, SKCanvas, SKBitmap, and SKPaint hold native resources. Implement or consume IDisposable and wrap with using (or await using for async equivalents). The compiler emits try/finally so Dispose runs on exceptions and returns. Do not wait for a finalizer — that is module 14 and too late for native memory under high-concurrency image work.
items.sixtySeconds: using owns IDisposable. SkiaSharp is native. Finalizers later. await using for async disposal.
